entries.original: As in11.2.1 the map theta(x)=-x′ is an automorphism of L, but this time it satisfies theta(e_r)=e_{-r} for each root r. To show that the fundamental co-roots and the root vectors e_r form a Chevalley basis we observe that theta(ie_r)=-(-ie_{-r}) and that [ie_r,-ie_{-r}]=h_r. Thus the fundamental co-roots together with ie_r (r positive) and -ie_{-r} (r positive) form a Chevalley basis, as in11.2.1. It follows that the fundamental co-roots together with e_r,e_{-r} (r positive) also form a Chevalley basis, using the general ideas of section4.2.
entries.corrected: After [h_r e_r]=2e_r: As in11.2.1 the map theta(x)=-x′ is an automorphism of L satisfying theta(e_r)=-e_{-r} for each root r. Thus the fundamental co-roots together with the root vectors e_r form a Chevalley basis, by the argument of11.2.1.
entries.reason: The imaginary rescaling detour rests on E045 and is false for the displayed matrices. With r=epsilon1-epsilon2, s=epsilon2-epsilon3, the displayed basis has [e_r,e_s]=e_{r+s}; scaling all positive-root vectors by i produces structure constant i, not plus/minus1. The corrected transpose sign directly gives N_{-r,-s}=-N_{r,s}. Together with the normalized co-roots and4.1.2 this gives N_{r,s}=plus/minus(p+1), exactly the valid argument of11.2.1. No imaginary rescaling is needed. This is an explicit proof repair, not just punctuation; full original paragraph retained here.
